entries.reason: Dawn mist is drawn at first light, so a society in a world at dawn starts its day at six in the morning.

licence.content_source: Authored for the Exulanica society clock; see the entry reason

entries.reason: A clear noon sky stands the sun high, so a society in a world at noon starts its day at midday and its clock reads twelve under that sun.

licence.content_source: Authored for the Exulanica society clock; see the entry reason

entries.reason: An overcast sky reads as grey daylight, so a society under it starts its day at ten in the morning; a dawn hour under a day's grey would be false.

licence.content_source: Authored for the Exulanica society clock; see the entry reason

entries.reason: Dusk lights the world from its look's evening, the sun low in the west, so a society in a world at dusk starts its day at six in the evening and its clock reads the hour its sky shows.

licence.content_source: Authored for the Exulanica society clock; see the entry reason

entries.reason: Thick fog hides the sun at any hour, so a society in a fogbound world starts its day at six in the morning, as the policy's own day does.

licence.content_source: Authored for the Exulanica society clock; see the entry reason

entries.reason: Night is drawn after dark, so a society in a world at night starts its day at half past nine in the evening, the hour its sky shows.

licence.content_source: Authored for the Exulanica society clock; see the entry reason

entries.reason: A world with no sky of its setting is lit by its look's own day; where that sun stands east of south (azimuth under 180 degrees) it is the morning's, so its society starts at ten in the morning.

licence.content_source: Authored for the Exulanica society clock; see the entry reason

entries.reason: Where the look's own day sun stands due south or west of it (azimuth from 180 degrees) it is the afternoon's, so a society in a world with no sky of its setting starts at three in the afternoon.

licence.content_source: Authored for the Exulanica society clock; see the entry reason
